title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Discover the functional student spaces and quiet retreats across Aurora University's campus that go beyond the standard tour highlights.

cards.title: Collaborative Zone at Phillips
cards.subtitle: Phillips Library
cards.notes: Use the rolling whiteboards to map out group projects or practice presentations in this high-energy collaborative space.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated area for group work featuring mobile whiteboards and flexible seating.
cards.evidence_claim: The first floor of Phillips Library encourages collaborative group work with rolling whiteboards for practicing presentations and group gathering.
cards.source_title: Student Services - Academic Catalogs < Aurora University
cards.access_notes: Open 96 hours per week during the regular semester; check library site for current daily hours.

cards.title: Quiet Retreat for Deep Focus
cards.subtitle: Phillips Library
cards.notes: Head upstairs to find individual study carrels and a strictly quiet environment perfect for exam prep and heavy reading.
cards.short_summary: A floor dedicated to silent, individual study with traditional carrels.
cards.evidence_claim: The second floor of Phillips Library is dedicated to individual work with study carrels and a quieter environment.
cards.source_title: Student Services - Academic Catalogs < Aurora University
cards.access_notes: Accessible during standard library operating hours.

cards.entity_name: Wackerlin Center for Faith and Action
cards.title: The Wackerlin Center Lounge
cards.subtitle: Wackerlin Center
cards.notes: Visit this center to study in a calm atmosphere or engage in volunteer and advocacy work with fellow students.
cards.short_summary: A multipurpose space for study, reflection, and community service coordination.
cards.evidence_claim: Students gather at the Wackerlin Center to study together, reflect, and engage in volunteer service and advocacy.
cards.source_title: Wackerlin Center for Faith and Action - Aurora University
cards.access_notes: Located at 430 S. Gladstone Ave; typically open during standard business hours.

cards.title: Social Hub at Stephens Hall
cards.subtitle: Stephens Hall Lower Level
cards.notes: Grab a quick bite and find a table in the lower level of Stephens Hall for a casual study session or social break.
cards.short_summary: A popular basement-level social space and casual study area with food options.
cards.evidence_claim: Located in the lower level of Stephens Hall, the Spot is a social gathering place and study area.
cards.source_title: Student Services - Academic Catalogs < Aurora University
cards.access_notes: Open to students with valid ID; check dining services for specific food service hours.

cards.title: Coffee and Collaboration
cards.subtitle: Institute for Collaboration
cards.notes: Set up your laptop at the Institute for Collaboration's first floor for a caffeinated study session near the coffee bar.
cards.short_summary: A modern study lounge located within the Institute for Collaboration building.
cards.evidence_claim: Tru Blu Coffee is located on the first floor of the Institute for Collaboration and offers specialty drinks and snacks.
cards.source_title: Student Services - Academic Catalogs < Aurora University
cards.access_notes: Accessible during building hours; coffee service hours vary by semester.

cards.title: The Dunham Hall Gallery
cards.subtitle: John C. Dunham Hall
cards.notes: Utilize the two-story atrium for informal gatherings or to view rotating exhibitions between classes.
cards.short_summary: A bright, open atrium used for social gatherings and art exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: A two-story atrium within Dunham Hall includes a central gallery and exhibition area for group or informal gatherings.

cards.title: Professional Prep Space
cards.subtitle: Hill Center for Student Success
cards.notes: Access career resources and quiet seating areas designed to help you focus on professional development and planning.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated space for career exploration and academic success planning.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hill Center for Student Success prepares students for careers through vocational exploration and career development programs.
cards.access_notes: Located at 1433 Prairie Street; south entrance access during construction.

cards.title: Quiet Reflection in Eckhart
cards.subtitle: Eckhart Hall Third Floor
cards.notes: Find a moment of silence for meditation or quiet reflection in this small chapel located on the top floor of Eckhart Hall.
cards.short_summary: A peaceful third-floor space for quiet reflection and faith-based events.
cards.evidence_claim: Located on the third floor of Eckhart Hall, faculty, staff, and students use this space for quiet reflection.
cards.access_notes: Open for quiet use when not reserved for religious services or events.

cards.title: Art-Inspired Study Nook
cards.subtitle: Hill Welcome Center
cards.notes: Study surrounded by Native American art and artifacts in the museum's dedicated classroom and study center spaces.
cards.short_summary: A unique study environment integrated within the campus art museum.
cards.evidence_claim: The Schingoethe Center features state-of-the-art exhibition spaces combined with a lecture hall, classroom space, and study center.
cards.access_notes: Free admission; check seasonal museum hours as it closes for summer and winter breaks.

cards.title: Music Practice Rooms
cards.subtitle: Parolini Music Center
cards.notes: Utilize the practice rooms and rehearsal spaces in this dedicated music facility for individual or small group practice.
cards.short_summary: The campus hub for music performance, rehearsal, and practice.
cards.evidence_claim: The Parolini Music Center is a primary facility for the music department's ensembles and student practice.
cards.access_notes: Primarily for music students; check with the department for general student access policies.
